title: Knowledge Check 3 — Lessons 11-15
description: Pooled check over Lessons 11-15 of the AI at Work series. Score 80% or higher to unlock the cert prep practice exam.

questions.question: What is Lesson 11's division of labor between you and the AI tool?
options: You bring facts and judgment; AI brings the fluent first pass
AI brings facts; you bring fluency
questions.explanation: Lesson 11: you bring the facts and judgment; AI brings the fluent first pass.

questions.question: What caution does Lesson 11 draw from the HBR summary example?
options: AI always catches the key data point
AI output gravitates to familiar ideas and can miss a critical shift
questions.explanation: Lesson 11: AI output gravitates to the most familiar, defensible ideas, as in the president example where a sales mix shift was nearly missed.

questions.question: What leave-out line is critical in the worked client email?
options: Make it as long as possible
Do not add any numbers, dates, or promises I did not give you
Invent a positive reason for delays
questions.explanation: Lesson 11: the leave-out line prevents the tool from inventing numbers, dates, or promises.

questions.question: What are the two distinct jobs Lesson 12 describes?
options: The two distinct jobs are editing what is there and reviewing before it ships.
questions.explanation: Lesson 12: editing (fixing what's there) and reviewing (checking before it ships).

questions.question: Why is shipping an edited-but-unreviewed draft dangerous?
options: A beautifully edited draft can still be wrong, and it looks done so it ships on autopilot
Editing is not a real skill
questions.explanation: Lesson 12: a beautifully edited draft can be completely wrong, and looking done causes the reviewing gate to be skipped.

questions.question: What is provenance in Lesson 12?
options: Provenance is where a piece of information came from.
questions.explanation: Lesson 12: provenance is where information came from — you cannot check a claim with no origin.

questions.question: What is the single biggest lever in AI research?
options: Giving the tool the actual documents to work from
Letting the tool search on its own
questions.explanation: Lesson 13: give the tool your actual documents (grounding/RAG) instead of relying on its memory.

questions.question: What question should you ask to force disagreements between sources?
options: What do these sources agree on?
Where do these sources disagree, and what exactly does each one say?
Which source is the most famous?
questions.explanation: Lesson 13: ask for the disagreement, because a decision usually rests on a difference, not a similarity.

questions.question: Why does cleaning come before analysis in Lesson 14?
options: Because analysis is only as good as the table it runs on
Because cleaning is the most interesting part
Because the tool cannot read messy data
questions.explanation: Lesson 14: analysis is only as good as the table it runs on; messy data yields confident wrong totals.

questions.question: What share of a data project is spent cleaning, per Lesson 14?
options: Roughly 80 percent of a data project is spent on cleaning and organizing data.
questions.explanation: Lesson 14 cites roughly 80 percent of a data project spent on cleaning and organizing data.

questions.question: What is the most-cited fix for a good meeting?
options: Setting a clear agenda is the most-cited fix for making a meeting productive.
questions.explanation: Lesson 15: 67 percent of professionals named setting a clear agenda as what makes a good meeting.

questions.question: What is the difference between an action item with no owner and one with an owner?
options: No owner is a wish; an owner is a commitment
An owner only matters for large projects
questions.explanation: Lesson 15: an action item with no owner is a wish; one with an owner is a commitment.
